# Digital4Better Open Data — complete npm package reference

> Offline usage documentation for the reference datasets shipped in `@digital4better/data`. Data are plain JSON and CSV files. They support environmental modeling; many values are references or estimates rather than direct measurements.

## Scope and version

This reference describes the collections in this package. Read [package.json](./package.json) for the installed version and [README.md](./README.md) for an overview and source families. The [website](https://digital4better.github.io/data/) and its [catalog](https://digital4better.github.io/data/catalog.json) can change independently of an installed package. Verify online examples and file inventories against the local files. Reading these local datasets requires no account or network connection.

There is no exported query function or runtime service. Open the desired file under `data/`. JSON preserves nested objects, arrays and source keys. CSV is a tabular projection: some nested fields are omitted and lists can use `|` separators. Use JSON for complete structured records. Do not infer a field is absent from JSON merely because CSV omits it.

## Finding the right data

1. Identify the collection matching the question. Electricity impact factors are in `factor`; electricity technology shares are in `mix`; cloud regions are in `cloud`; geographic identifiers are in `country`.
2. Inspect the collection's file inventory. Opening one file does not establish the coverage of the whole package.
3. For temporal data, select geography, yearly or monthly granularity, and actual-mix or renewable-only scenario explicitly.
4. Check that the exact source key, requested period and requested indicator are present and usable. File-level availability is not record-level availability. Inspect each file rather than assuming all variants have identical coverage.
5. If the requested record is unavailable, report the file and keys checked. A result can be absent even when the collection exists. Do not silently turn an absent value into zero or use another territory, period or scenario.
6. If the consuming application authorizes a fallback, record the requested and selected geography/period, source file, indicator and reason. A search may proceed from subdivision to country, continent and world, but broader averages are substitutions, not equivalent observations. There is no universally correct fallback order across time and geography.

Use the exact identifiers in each source file. Cloud files can use lowercase country codes and aliases; electricity country keys use source country identifiers. Do not apply one collection's identifier normalization blindly to another. Geographic mappings are provided in `data/country/`; confirm membership from the actual records.

## Collection guides

The following guides are included in the package. Each is the detailed reference for its file inventory, schema, column units, methodology, source attribution and limitations; consult it alongside the usage examples below.

| Collection | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Electricity impacts | [factor](./data/factor/README.md) |
| Electricity shares and historical-series rules | [mix](./data/mix/README.md) |
| Generation technology impacts | [energy](./data/energy/README.md) |
| Equipment power and allocated impacts | [equipment](./data/equipment/README.md) |
| Geographic identifiers and distances | [country](./data/country/README.md) |
| Cloud infrastructure and host allocation | [cloud](./data/cloud/README.md) |
| AI models and estimated characteristics | [ai](./data/ai/README.md) |
| Building electricity and fuels | [facility](./data/facility/README.md) |
| Employee travel | [transport](./data/transport/README.md) |

## Historical electricity references

Historical country series can be retained and carried forward when a territory is absent from current upstream exports. These are not new observations. The [mix methodology](./data/mix/README.md#missing-periods-and-historical-references) defines retention, precedence and aggregation limits for both mixes and factors.

[electricity-provenance.json](./scripts/electricity-provenance.json) is maintenance metadata, not a dataset: it records the pinned snapshot, territories and period coverage. It is stored alongside the history script and included in npm for offline interpretation. Original observation dates can be unknown; package release dates are not measurement dates.

## Missing values, zero and time

- A missing property, `null` or an empty CSV cell denotes unavailable data. Preserve that distinction in calculations and exports.
- An explicit numeric zero must be preserved. Some provider or hardware zeros are dataset conventions, not independently verified zero environmental impacts; review the relevant assumptions.
- Do not use truthiness checks such as `if (!value)` to detect absence: that also rejects numeric zero. Check null/undefined and the value's type explicitly.
- Years are string keys such as `2025`; months are string keys such as `2025-01`. Do not silently mix annual and monthly series.
- The current year can be partial. Available periods may contain estimated or carried-forward values; they do not guarantee new observations. The current series do not individually flag all filled values.
- File modification dates, package release dates and source observation dates have different meanings. A daily rebuild does not mean every source was refreshed.
- For reproducibility, retain the exact package version or file snapshot, source keys, period, indicator, unit and any fallback. Public download URLs can change.

## Units and environmental impact indicators

Read the collection guide and each record's functional unit before calculating. Environmental impacts combine an indicator's numerator with the activity denominator: for example, climate change `gwp` is kg CO2 eq/kWh for electricity, but kg CO2 eq/pkm or /vkm for transport.

- Electricity generation and consumption factors are per kWh, but describe different boundaries.
- Equipment power in W is not energy in kWh; equipment embodied factors in `/s` are already time-allocated.
- Cloud manufacturing impacts are in tCO2e before time amortization, not kg CO2 eq per second.
- Transport `pkm` and `vkm` require different passenger/vehicle activity data.
- Characterized water impacts (`wu`) are not physical litres, and cloud `wue` has a different boundary.
- Do not sum unlike impact categories or overlapping climate totals/components.

Indicator definitions and units are maintained in the collection guides rather than repeated here.

## Electricity impact factors: `data/factor/`

Files use `<geography>-<frequency>[-green].json`, with matching CSV files:

- Geography: `subdivision`, `country`, `continent`, `world`.
- Frequency: `yearly`, `monthly`.
- Scenario: no suffix for the modeled full mix; `-green` for the renewable-only scenario.

For example, [subdivision-yearly.json](./data/factor/subdivision-yearly.json) and [subdivision-monthly.json](./data/factor/subdivision-monthly.json) contain sub-national series. Reading only [country-yearly.json](./data/factor/country-yearly.json) is insufficient to determine whether sub-national factors exist. Coverage of one subdivision does not imply coverage of all subdivisions or periods.

Country, continent and subdivision JSON use `{ territory: { period: { indicator: value } } }`. World JSON uses `{ period: { indicator: value } }`, without an extra world wrapper. Check the existing continent names instead of assuming continent codes are used as time-series keys.

The shared indicators are `adpe` (resource use, minerals and metals), `ap` (acidification), `ctue` (freshwater ecotoxicity), `ctuh-c` and `ctuh-nc` (human toxicity, cancer and non-cancer), `gwp` (climate change), `ir` (ionising radiation), `pm` (particulate matter) and `wu` (water use). These are distinct impact categories with different native units. Electricity factors are per kWh; `gwp` is in kg CO2 equivalent/kWh. Check the source methodology for other indicator units and characterization methods before combining datasets. Do not infer physical liters of water from a water-impact indicator or add different impact categories together.

Impact = electricity consumption in kWh × factor per kWh. Educational example: 100 kWh × 0.05 kg CO2e/kWh = 5 kg CO2e. The example factor is fictional; read the dataset value for a real calculation.

Node.js example in a project that depends on this package:

```js
const factors = require('@digital4better/data/data/factor/subdivision-yearly.json');
const territory = 'CA-QC';
const period = '2023';
const factor = factors[territory]?.[period]?.gwp;
if (typeof factor !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(factor)) {
  throw new Error(`No usable gwp factor for ${territory} / ${period}`);
}
const result = { territory, period, factor, kWh: 100, kgCO2e: 100 * factor };
```

### Methodology and scenarios

The [factor guide](./data/factor/README.md) documents columns and per-kWh units. The [mix methodology](./data/mix/README.md#methodology) defines imports, aggregation, renewable-only scenarios and fallback rules shared by both collections. Green files are hypothetical scenarios, not actual supply or contract certificates; unavailable green values are not zero impacts.

## Electricity mixes: `data/mix/`

The same geography/frequency/scenario filename combinations and temporal nesting apply. Values are dimensionless shares, normally between 0 and 1, not percentages. Use [country-yearly.json](./data/mix/country-yearly.json) for territorial series and [world-monthly.json](./data/mix/world-monthly.json) for period-keyed world values. The [mix guide](./data/mix/README.md) is the reference for technology names, sources and historical coverage limits.

## Cloud infrastructure: `data/cloud/`

Each provider has `<provider>-regions`, `<provider>-vms` and `<provider>-hosts` files in JSON and CSV. Shared `cpus` and `accelerators` catalogs describe hardware. JSON roots are arrays. The [cloud guide](./data/cloud/README.md) maintains the complete schemas, provider-specific capacity conventions, regional metrics, source URLs and assumption codes.

Join VM `host` to the same provider's host `id`; CPU and accelerator references join to the shared catalogs. Prefer VM `embodied_allocated`, in tCO2e before time amortization. VM `embodied` is deprecated and has heterogeneous historical scope; host `embodied` is the total modeled host impact and is not deprecated.

Allocation is `embodied_allocated = host.embodied / host_instances`. The count describes modeled homogeneous packing, not observed occupancy. Do not allocate the host fraction twice. Apply lifetime and usage-duration allocation separately. The [methodology](./data/cloud/README.md#methodology) owns the calculation formula and conservative residual-capacity policy.

Profiles are calculation scenarios, not a physical-server inventory. Native GB/GiB conventions are retained; CPU alternatives are not socket counts. Hardware TDP is a thermal envelope, not measured workload power. Provider zeros and proxies need interpretation, including Google's CFE rather than renewable matching. Historical listings do not guarantee availability. Missing values remain unavailable.

Maintenance inputs and evidence are in the repository's [sources/cloud](https://github.com/digital4better/data/tree/main/sources/cloud), outside published datasets; the [calculator](https://github.com/digital4better/data/blob/main/scripts/cloud-hosts.ts) is not shipped in npm.

## AI models: `data/ai/`

[models.json](./data/ai/models.json) is an array of model records; [models.csv](./data/ai/models.csv) is its tabular projection.

- `name`, `vendor`, `type`, `architecture`: source identifiers and model classification.
- `pattern`: a name-recognition expression, not a provider API endpoint.
- `parameters.active` and `parameters.total`: active and total parameters in billions. Distinguish these for mixture-of-experts architectures.
- `context`: context capacity in tokens, not a guaranteed output length.
- `input`, `output`: supported modalities.
- `reasoning`, `tools`: recorded capabilities.
- `providers`: hosting-provider identifiers and variants, not universal identifiers.
- `estimated`: fields identified as estimates. Check it before presenting parameters or context as vendor disclosures.
- `sources`: URLs for provenance and further verification.
- `open`: an openness flag; it does not substitute for the model's license.

Not every model has every field. Legacy models and historical/restricted provider references can remain. Check current provider availability separately. Model size alone is insufficient to calculate environmental impacts; no per-model environmental footprint is supplied. Preserve upstream attribution for adapted estimates. This includes EcoLogits contributors and Samuel Rince where their estimates or family proxies are retained; do not present these as vendor disclosures. Read the [AI guide](./data/ai/README.md), [parameter provenance](./data/ai/provenance.md) and [cloud coverage inventory](./data/ai/cloud-coverage.md) for their boundaries and unresolved historical assumptions.

## Equipment: `data/equipment/`

[energy.json](./data/equipment/energy.json) and [embodied.json](./data/equipment/embodied.json) are category-keyed objects with CSV counterparts. Energy entries use `description`, `value` and `unit`; embodied entries contain environmental indicators and their allocation unit. Use the [equipment guide](./data/equipment/README.md) for the complete indicator table and network conventions.

For power in W, `kWh = value / 1000 * operating hours`. For an embodied factor in `/s`, multiply by usage seconds; do not apply lifetime allocation again. These generic references are not provider-specific cloud VM footprints.

## Energy technologies: `data/energy/`

[energy-impacts.json](./data/energy/energy-impacts.json) maps technology names to lifecycle impact factors per kWh generated; CSV adds the `energy` key column. The [energy guide](./data/energy/README.md) defines indicators, units and lifecycle sources. These factors are inputs to mix modeling, not consumption factors or power-plant measurements.

## Building energy: `data/facility/`

[factors.json](./data/facility/factors.json) is an array of annual records with CSV projection. Select `id`, `location` and `period`; read `unit`, indicators, `source` and `sourceUrl`. The [facility guide](./data/facility/README.md) documents identifiers, source mappings and lifecycle boundaries. Match fuel PCI/PCS calorific bases to the input activity. Electricity is synchronized with annual grid factors; fuel periods may differ. Do not invent missing geographic equivalents.

## Transport: `data/transport/`

[factors.json](./data/transport/factors.json) is an array of annual references with CSV projection. Select `id`, `location` and `period`, then inspect `unit`, indicators and source fields. The [transport guide](./data/transport/README.md) documents modes, units, exclusions and aviation assumptions. Passenger-km and vehicle-km require explicit occupancy conversion; `location` is a reference context, not the trip's origin or destination.

## Geographic references: `data/country/`

The [geography guide](./data/country/README.md) inventories country, continent, region, map and distance files and owns their identifier and distance conventions. Geographic catalogs are arrays; SVG paths and distance references are identifier-keyed objects. Distance CSV files separate origin/destination columns. Do not split every composite JSON key into two-character codes.

Distances are km-based proxies, not measured routes or latency. Geographic membership and map outlines do not establish electricity-data coverage.

## Reuse, attribution and online references

The database is licensed under [ODbL 1.0](./LICENCE). Read the license for reuse, attribution and sharing conditions. Preserve source URLs, assumptions and any upstream credits accompanying adapted data. Suggested dataset attribution: Digital4Better Open Data — collection/file — installed package version — ODbL 1.0 — https://github.com/digital4better/data.

Useful online entry points:

- [Website documentation index](https://digital4better.github.io/data/llms.txt).
- [Complete website reference](https://digital4better.github.io/data/llms-full.txt).
- [Current website catalog](https://digital4better.github.io/data/catalog.json), with dataset fields, coverage summaries and absolute download URLs. It describes the deployed site, not necessarily this installed package.
- [English methodology](https://digital4better.github.io/data/en/methodology/) and [French methodology](https://digital4better.github.io/data/fr/methodology/).
- [English electricity guide](https://digital4better.github.io/data/en/guides/electricity/), [cloud metrics guide](https://digital4better.github.io/data/en/guides/cloud-metrics/) and [AI models guide](https://digital4better.github.io/data/en/guides/ai-models/).
- [Repository and issue tracker](https://github.com/digital4better/data).
